issue.title: Share one proven history catalog across ordered multi-target bead work
issue.description: Each target of an ordered multi-target 'sase bead work' run still pays its own bounded full-history discovery pass; four 40k-history fresh epics measured 96.6s vs the 90s local-orchestration goal in sase-xr.6's acceptance benchmark. Proposal and freshness-proof constraints in the proposal field.

task_type_fields.proposal:
Share one proven history catalog across the ordered targets of a multi-target `sase bead work` invocation, so each later target pays an incremental freshness proof instead of its own full bounded discovery pass.

Proposed by phase bead sase-xr.6 (epic sase-xr, "Make epic launches and relaunches scale with the requested work"). The epic's acceptance benchmark hit every single-epic target with wide margins (fresh 40k/12 median 25.1s vs the 45s target, ~19x vs the required 10x), but the four-ordered-epic 40k case measured 96.6s (n=1) against the 90s local-orchestration goal — see artifact file:explicit:8f8265e7880b018d112e5370. The residual cost is structural: each target runs its own bounded O(H) discovery/catalog pass (17 full-scan marks for four targets vs 5 for one), exactly as the epic's per-target complexity contract specifies.

The work needs an explicit ownership/freshness-proof design for carrying a proven catalog across target boundaries: epic sase-xr's plan deliberately requires refreshing mutable ownership/bead data at each target boundary and forbids reusing snapshots across mutations without proof, and earlier targets' own cleanup/spawn effects invalidate parts of the catalog. A workable design likely reconciles the shared catalog with the known effects of completed targets (the batch planner already returns exact per-target effects) rather than rescanning history, while keeping destructive checks fresh and the stop-at-first-error/partial-retry contracts intact. Validate with the existing `just bench-epic-launch` ordered_four_target_batch scenario at 40k history.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Out of scope for epic sase-xr because the epic's chosen complexity contract is "a constant number of O(H) discovery/proof passes per target plus O(K + R) indexed lookups", which the landed work meets; sharing a catalog across ordered targets crosses the plan's explicit constraint that mutable ownership/bead data be refreshed at each target boundary and that snapshots never be reused across mutations without an ownership/freshness proof. Designing that proof is new work, not remediation of the epic (the 7% four-target miss is an n=1 sample of pre-existing per-target cost the epic already reduced from 780s/3 targets in production to 96.6s/4 targets isolated at 40k history).
